questions.prompt: A streamed reply ends with stop reason max_tokens. What does that tell your program?
options: The model finished its answer normally
The request used more tokens than the context window
The reply reached the max_tokens limit, so the text is probably cut off
The model wants to stream a second reply
questions.explanation: max_tokens means the model stopped because it reached the length limit, not because it finished. The text is probably incomplete. A finished answer ends with end_turn.

questions.prompt: Why does the stream reader keep a buffer instead of parsing each piece of text it receives?
options: A piece of network data can end in the middle of a message, so only complete messages are parsed
JSON.parse can only read one character at a time
The provider sends every message twice
The buffer stores the conversation for the next request
questions.explanation: A message ends with an empty line, but network data can split it anywhere. The reader waits for the empty line before it parses the message.

questions.prompt: In which part of the stream does the stop reason arrive?
questions.explanation: The model only knows why it stopped when it stops. The stop reason comes in message_delta, just before message_stop.
